You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To see the forest, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Check local weather patterns for optimal visibility (1 hour)
Step 2. Apply high-strength insect repellent (5 minutes)
Step 3. Research various national park trail maps (3 hours)
Step 4. Purchase a durable pair of hiking boots (2 hours)
Step 5. Pack a lightweight emergency shelter (20 minutes)
Step 6. Fill a three-liter water bladder (10 minutes)
Step 7. Ascend to the final panoramic lookout point (1 hour)
Step 8. Identify the main trailhead entrance (15 minutes)
Step 9. Begin the steep mountain ascent (4 hours)
Step 10. Clean and calibrate your binoculars (15 minutes)
Step 11. Break in the new hiking boots on a short walk (3 days)
Step 12. Check the batteries in your GPS device (5 minutes)
Step 13. Confirm the park’s seasonal opening hours (10 minutes)

Step 61. Take a deep breath of the forest air (1 minute)

Step 63. Sit quietly to appreciate the total silence (15 minutes)

Step 65. Put on moisture-wicking socks (5 minutes)
Step 66. Watch a tutorial on mountain navigation (1 hour)
Step 67. Signal your position to a partner (1 minute)
Step 68. Pack a small trowel for waste (5 minutes)

Step 70. Verify the fuel level in the vehicle (5 minutes)
Step 71. Put on a wide-brimmed hat (2 minutes)
Step 72. Eat a slow-release energy bar (10 minutes)
Step 73. Stow your electronics in dry bags (15 minutes)
Step 74. Check the integrity of your tent stakes (10 minutes)
Step 75. Buy a souvenir patch from the visitor center (10 minutes)
Step 76. Pack a pair of binoculars (5 minutes)
Step 77. Look for animal tracks in the mud (20 minutes)
Step 78. Drive to the park entrance gates (2 hours)
Step 79. Adjust your backpack's hip belt (2 minutes)

Step 81. Follow the blue trail markers (2 hours)
Step 82. Estimate the height of the canopy (15 minutes)
Step 83. Park the car in the designated lot (10 minutes)
Step 84. Gather all necessary permits and IDs (30 minutes)
Step 85. Check the trail sign for distance updates (5 minutes)
Step 86. Note the change in air temperature (5 minutes)
Step 87. Read the "Leave No Trace" guidelines (20 minutes)
Step 88. Replace old shoelaces with paracord (15 minutes)
Step 89. Check for ticks on your clothing (10 minutes)
Step 90. Take a panoramic photo of the valley (5 minutes)
Step 91. Study the moss growth on the north side of trees (15 minutes)
Step 92. Ascend above the treeline (3 hours)
Step 93. Compare the leaf shapes of different species (20 minutes)
Step 94. Pack a signal mirror (5 minutes)
Step 95. Sign the trail register at the trailhead (5 minutes)
Step 96. Observe the play of light through the leaves (20 minutes)
Step 97. Zip up all pockets on your jacket (2 minutes)
Step 98. Pause to listen to a nearby stream (10 minutes)
Step 99. Wipe the sweat from your forehead (1 minute)
Step 100. Reach the summit of the tallest hill (1 hour)
